title: Mitered squares lap throw
subtitle: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw assembled from 20 cm mitered squares in DK.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw made from thirty 20 cm mitered squares, each worked from the corner out using k2tog decreases to form the diagonal. Squares are joined as they are knitted. Uses approximately 50 g of DK per square across a range of colours.
sourceNotes: Knit-on-together (shadow knitting) mitered square construction is described in Barbara Walker's A Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1968), §Mitred Square Stitch. Elizabeth Zimmermann, Knitting Without Tears (1971), §Modular Knitting, describes the same join-as-you-go assembly method for blankets.

glossaryTerms.definition: A knitted square worked from two adjacent corners toward the centre diagonal, using paired k2tog decreases in the centre on every RS row. The decreases create a visible diagonal line across the square. Once the single remaining stitch is reached, the square is complete. Adjacent squares are cast on from the live stitches of completed neighbours, eliminating sewing.

content.text: Thirty 20 cm
mitered squares
worked in garter stitch on 4 mm needles and assembled join-as-you-go into a 5-square by 6-square 100 by 120 cm lap throw.

This throw is a modular project: each square is a separate unit that can be worked at any time and stored, making it the ideal travel project. The join-as-you-go method means no sewing; each new square picks up stitches from the live edge of its neighbours. Colour changes happen per square; no yarn needs to be carried across a long row. Budget about 50 g (about 110 m / 120 yards) per square for 30 squares in DK across any number of colours. Total: approximately 1,500 g in assorted DK colours.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: Approximately 50 g per square × 30 squares = 1,500 g total in DK weight across any mix of colours. Contrast squares make the mitered diagonal more visible.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) needles, straight or circular 60 cm or longer

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 2 per square (to mark the centre decrease position)

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles. Each 20 cm square casts on 87 stitches (44 stitches per side plus 1 centre stitch) and decreases to 1 stitch over 43 RS rows.

If your garter stitch gauge is 20 per 10 cm, cast on 79 stitches per square for the same 20 cm finished size. At 24 per 10 cm, cast on 97 stitches. Adjust the centre-stitch position accordingly (centre = (cast-on - 1) / 2).
Stitches used

items.name: CDD
items.qty: central double decrease: sl2 knitwise together, k1, pass 2 slipped sts over, reduces 3 sts to 1 at the exact centre

content.text: Pattern
First square
Cast on 87 stitches. Long-tail tail: (4 × 87) / 10 + 15 = 34.8 + 15 = 50 cm. Measure 60 cm. Place marker after stitch 43 and before stitch 45 (the centre stitch is stitch 44).
RS rows: k to 1 stitch before marker, CDD (using the marker stitch and one stitch either side), k to end. 2 stitches decreased per RS row.
WS rows: knit all. Continue until 1 stitch remains. Cut yarn and pull through.
Subsequent squares (join-as-you-go)

Pick up 44 stitches along the edge of a completed neighbour, cast on 43 new stitches for the other half, place centre marker, and work as the first square. The pick-up edge becomes one side of the new square; the cast-on forms the other.
Stitch count check-ins

After row 22 of any square (the midpoint): count across. You should have 41 stitches (87 - 2 × 23 = 41, with rows starting from 0). This confirms the decrease rate is correct before the second half of the square. After row 43: 1 stitch should remain.
Common faults

Squares not measuring 20 cm: worked at a different gauge than swatched. Mitered squares must be swatched at the exact gauge before starting; adjusting the cast-on count per the gauge note above will correct the size.
CDD creating a visible hole at the centre: the slip was worked knitwise individually rather than both together. Slip 2 knitwise at once (both onto the needle in one motion) to avoid twisting them.
Assembly order
Work in rows from bottom left to bottom right (5 squares), then second row left to right, and so on. Each interior square shares two edges with previously completed neighbours.
Finishing
Weave in ends from each square. There are no seams to sew. If the outer edges of the border squares have loose cast-on edges, work a simple garter pickup row around the perimeter.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

From plain mitered squares, try working each square in two colours alternating every two rows: the diagonal shows in one colour and the two triangles in another. No additional techniques are required; only the colour change at the left edge is new.
